card.name: Small words in old literary prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words (with, to, from, into, on, well, un) inside archaic, formal or literary prose, such as old hymns, historical essays and legal rhetoric. It appears where the next word continues a flowing phrase.

modes.label: Prepositions in elevated prose
modes.description: Prepositions like with, to, from, into and on in the middle of a stately sentence.
modes.example: Lead on O King Eternal, we follow not<< with>> fears! For gladness breaks like morning

modes.label: Start of a hyphenated or prefixed word
modes.description: Well or un opening a compound that continues, as in well-known or unheeded.
modes.example: is founded on<< well>>-known principles of the civil law, by
